content.text: Check health of our infrastructure and flag any issues
Our gcp project named emisar. Check health of everything.

A health report flagged "Livebook has zero instances." Check this conclusion against the intended configuration in the available repository. Is this enough to call it an infrastructure issue? Cite the code you actually inspect and distinguish checked-in intent from any live deployment evidence. Keep the answer concise. This is read-only local Lab acceptance: do not change repository source code or infrastructure, and do not send Slack posts, reactions, typing/status, files, or any external communications.

public_responses.message:
The main application, registry, and database look healthy in the checks performed, but Livebook has no serving capacity and several resilience/monitoring issues need attention.

Findings, in priority order:

1. **Livebook has zero instances.** Its group stayed at 0 throughout the sampled 30 minutes, and both Livebook backends returned empty health lists. If Livebook should be available, restore its serving capacity. [Group-size evidence](https://emisar.dev/app/emisar/runs/01a074a7-b398-7c4d-aad9-a79106a4db6b)
2. **No zone redundancy for the application or database.** Both healthy portal VMs are in us-central1-a. Cloud SQL is ZONAL in us-central1-c with no standby. These are resilience risks, not current outages. [VM placement](https://emisar.dev/app/emisar/runs/01a074a2-5930-7ffa-95c8-d5f797b25880) · [Database configuration](https://emisar.dev/app/emisar/runs/01a0749e-fdb8-775c-8bcc-1186d45ab6d5)
3. **Runner security/compatibility issues persist.** Both connected runners report descriptor_mismatch and signature enforcement disabled. The debugging and Docker packs are unavailable because of compatibility mismatches.
4. **Monitoring coverage is incomplete.** VM disk and memory queries returned no recent samples despite enabled alert policies. Error-log access returned HTTP 403, and storage inventory was denied storage.buckets.list. Consequently, I cannot certify host disk/memory or bucket health. [Missing disk samples](https://emisar.dev/app/emisar/runs/01a074a5-9ad0-78ab-a0c8-99af41992209) · [Missing memory samples](https://emisar.dev/app/emisar/runs/01a074a9-78a1-7896-9085-7cac2560d766)

Healthy observations:

- Main site and registry checks passed from all six monitoring locations in the sampled half hour; returned load-balancer metrics contained no 5xx responses.
- Both portal backends are HEALTHY; the managed group is stable at its target of 2. Both application runtimes respond and clocks are synchronized.
- SQL stayed up in the sampled hour. Five-minute averages show CPU around 14–17%, memory 55–56%, disk 5.7%, and transaction-ID utilization 0.2%.
- The latest seven backups succeeded; newest completed September 5 at 03:36 UTC. PITR is enabled. [Backups](https://emisar.dev/app/emisar/runs/01a074a2-d618-799e-a007-a68bb65b220d)
- All three managed certificates are ACTIVE; earliest expiry is October 10. NAT samples show no allocation failures, and the fleet-monitoring heartbeat is present.

The earlier degraded cloud-init boot records remain a follow-up; they do not establish a current network outage. This assessment covers the resources exposed by the available actions, not every possible GCP service. No configuration changes were made.

Evidence limitation: run links are available, but infrastructure tools supplied no source_ref for citation records; durable goal creation returned unauthorized.

No—zero instances alone is insufficient to call this an infrastructure issue.

At checked-in commit `86a85a97c471`, `infra/livebook.tf:69–76` creates a VM only when both `livebook_enabled` and `livebook_running` are true. `infra/variables.tf:231–240` defaults Livebook to disabled and explicitly supports parking it with `livebook_running=false`. The instance group intentionally becomes empty (`infra/livebook.tf:155–163`), and readiness waits are skipped when no VM is expected (`infra/load_balancer.tf:97–106`).

This establishes supported repository intent, not the deployed configuration. I did not verify live workspace variables or instance state. Confirm that deployment actually expects Livebook to run before classifying zero instances as a fault.
